nodes.label: Advisory Lock for Sync Serialization
nodes.rationale: pg_try_advisory_lock serializes nightly + manual OSSPA sync runs. The connection holding the lock must remain checked out from the pool for the entire sync to prevent a second sync from reusing the same session and reentrantly acquiring the lock.

nodes.label: Atomic Embedding Swap Pattern
nodes.rationale: Clear-old + write-new embedding runs in one transaction so a crash mid-write can never leave an item with zero or partial vectors, which would silently drop it from vector search. Prior vectors remain until the new set commits. This transaction commit also clears is_stale.

nodes.label: content_entities.status Universal Visibility Gate
nodes.rationale: Using Babylon's existing prod/event/dev vocabulary on content_entities.status means every retrieval query can filter without a per-source LEFT JOIN. One universal column serves both Babylon and OSSPA, and future content sources get the same column for free.

nodes.label: Content Hash Change Detection
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 of the full adoc body plus the CSV fields that feed the LLM prompt. Full body (not truncated prompt copy) so edits past osspa_max_adoc_bytes still trigger re-analysis. CSV prompt inputs included so a metadata-only edit re-triggers analysis without --force. Fields not in the prompt (Image1Url) do not force re-analysis.

nodes.label: Portfolio Architecture Terminology Rule
nodes.rationale: Never call OSSPA items 'reference architectures'. In Red Hat usage a reference architecture is a specific formally published prescriptive artifact. OSSPA assets are curated 'art of the possible' examples. Embedding text prefix is 'Portfolio architecture: ' not 'Reference architecture: ' — baked into every stored vector, changing it later forces full re-embed of all portfolio_arch rows.

nodes.label: Retire Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: retire_missing_osspa runs only if the new active-row count is >= osspa_retire_shrink_guard_pct (default 50%) of current non-retired portfolio_arch rows. HTTP 200 + parseable header proves request succeeded but not that the body is complete — a mid-stream truncation can still deliver valid non-empty CSV. The shrink guard catches that.
